element: the tipped glass of sugarcane juice at Aaru's right hand, together with the arc of juice already leaving its mouth
note:
Re-derived from scratch, because the sprite and patch already on disk for this slot were cut by an agent whose parameters were lost. Cut the FALLEN GLASS ONLY, juice arc included, and leave the full glass painted on the cart flank near (65,161) alone - that one is signwriting on the cart, not an object.

bg_strip is the haze and sand to the right of the glass. It has to start at 243 because the glass's base corner reaches x=236, and it has to stop at 285 because the card's rounded corner has already turned white at x=295 by row 196. Its per-row median sits 13-20/255 below the sand immediately left of the glass, which is nowhere near the d1>62 block, so the rough pass still hides the whole element from the interpolation.

art's x0 IS A WALL, not a measurement - the painted picture really starts at x=10. It is there because the second pass blocks only mask|guard, so the boy's leg and fist, which the first pass did block, come back as background samples and the sigma-7 row blur drags them right: the field landed 23/255 dark at x=200 and 19/255 dark along the arc's own left tip. This card cannot add a guard without editing the shared cutter, so x0=202 fences the boy out of the sampling instead, which is the same argument samosa_wall makes on 07-dog. Each row then interpolates between real sand at x=202..212 and real sand at x>=241, and the residual just left of the arc (x199..202, y158..168) fell from mean 19.4 / max 31.1 to mean 2.0 / max 5.9. y0, x1 and y1 are the defaults; the glass stops at y=196, five rows clear of the cream frame.

The refined field is very accurate on this card - clean sand and haze read a median of 1.8 and a p99 of 4.7 - which is what lets t_lo go down to 14, and it HAS to go there, because the glass is transparent above the juice line and its right wall is a single dark pixel reading only 20-53: (230,176) is (186,166,127) against a (228,201,153) field. The gap between the arc's left tip at y=158 and the boy's fist at y=152 is 5 rows of background reading 4-8, so nothing bridges at 14. At t_hi=60 the seed's core is the glass body; the arc's upper half is a separate core, but the grow through t_lo unions it, so one seed in the juice at (226,187), where d2 is 135, is enough and multi-seed is not needed.

close=5 is load-bearing. The empty top of the glass is optically invisible - field and card agree to within 7/255 at (231,174) - so the threshold bites a hole out of the upper-right corner and that hole OPENS to background across y=174..177, which fill_holes cannot shut. A 5px closing seals it into one solid glass silhouette. Do not raise it: the closing already swallows about five columns of pure background inside the mouth, where the painting shows no glass wall at all, and that background rides along with the sprite - an 11-degree turn moves it 5px and the background changes only 12/255 over 5px, so it stays invisible, but a bigger square would start filling the wedge of sky between the arc and the mouth as well.

sweep finds exactly three things: the 6px detached juice speck above the arc at (203..205,158..159), which reads d2 57 and cannot be reached by the grow because the row between it and the arc reads 7, and two lone rim pixels at (222,168) and (223,170). The patch erases all three; flying spray vanishing beats spray sitting still while the glass turns.

NO unmix, and that was A/B'd rather than assumed. Plain gives sprite@0 exactly 0.000 and, with the patch on, a residual against the field of 3.9 at 1px outside the mask and 9.0 at 3px, against sky noise of ~8 - so there is no standing outline to unmix away. unmix would have raised 317 rim pixels' alpha by up to 0.31 to stay in gamut, because this element is a soft-edged painted splash with a long low-contrast perimeter, and the moved sprite was indistinguishable from the plain one. Not worth hardening the rim for.

MOTION is a tilt: 0,0 and -11 degrees about (231,193), so the base stays planted and only the mouth swings. The origin is the midpoint of the base edge, measured off the mask's bottom, which runs from (236,190) to (227,196). Negative because the glass has to go FURTHER over, anticlockwise on screen, and that carries about 5px of mouth travel. Do NOT push past -12: the juice arc is part of the sprite and its tip closes on the boy's shorts - 5.0px clear at -11, 4.0px at -12, 3.0px at -14. The back-out ease peaks at 1.08 of the rotation, so -11 transiently reaches -11.9 and still clears by 4.1px, and the overshoot reads as the glass rocking on its base.

HD PASS. "hd": 3 moves this cut off the 311x212 screenshot crop and onto scratchpad/cards-hd/06-cart.png, 932x637, rendered at 3x from assets/rounds/r3-cart.webp at a gain of 2.408 native pixels per card pixel - so the detail is really there and is not an upscale. The recap pops this card to 3x, where the old 42x47 sprite was being blown up from a source with no more detail; the new one is 129x141, 3.07x by 3.00x, and app.js still places it by the 1x box because .pspr-art is width/height 100% of a wrap sized from that box.

EVERY NUMBER ABOVE IS THE 1x NUMBER, unchanged. The cutter multiplies the coordinate-bearing ones by 3 itself (see _hd_spec): seed, bg_strip, art, pad_box, pad_patch, close, feather, sweep's radius - and sweep's max_px by 3*3, because it is an AREA and scaling it by 3 alone would have silently stopped sweeping the juice speck, which is 6px at 1x and 54px here. t_hi and t_lo are colour distances and are NOT scaled: nothing about the RGB changed, and the refined field is if anything more accurate at 3x - clean background inside the art reads p50 1.09 / p99 4.70 against 1.73 / 17.72 at 1x, so t_lo=14 has more headroom than it did, not less.

THE BOX MOVED BY ONE 1x PIXEL, x0 199 -> 198, and app.js line ~5218 still says 199. The HD box is snapped outwards to a multiple of 3 so it divides back to whole 1x pixels - without that the sprite lands up to half a card pixel off - and 596 floors to 594 = 198*3. y0/x1/y1 land on multiples already. org '50% 96%' in app.js is unaffected in kind: under the 43px-wide box it means x=219.5 instead of 220.

WHAT THE HD PASS EXPOSED. Test (c) came out at 10.7 against a noise floor of 8, where the 1x cut had 2.4, and it was not the field: the max sat on the outermost ring of the footprint at a_patch 0.868, i.e. 13% of the original glass still standing as a 1px rim. `grown` is a city-block dilation, so at a convex corner of the silhouette the nearest outside pixel is nearer than pad_patch and the distance-transform alpha never reaches 1 - a shortfall proportional to pad, invisible at pad 3 (0.943) and visible at pad 9. Fixed in the shared cutter by one line, a_patch = max(a_patch, footprint), which is what the file's own header already promised; test (c) is now 0.00 and it was A/B'd against every other card in the table, none of which moves (all the unmix cards already force alpha to 1 over `reach`). Cost: test (b)'s mean over the box went 0.319 -> 0.330, because the sprite's soft rim now composites against field instead of card on that one ring. Still no unmix - the same A/B as at 1x holds.

VERIFIED AT 3x: patch alpha is exactly 0 on the whole canvas border and sprite alpha is exactly 0 there too, so there is no rectangle and nothing is clipped by the box; sprite-over-card at zero offset is 0.0000; a 12x-amplified difference of patched against card is confined to the glass-and-arc silhouette with a soft feather dying to black inside the canvas; and at 4x the patched sand is a smooth gradient with no seam and no ghost of the glass. zoom dropped 6 -> 2, which is the same on-screen magnification as 6 was at 1x.

NO art_hd HERE, and that was checked rather than assumed. The hd card's cream frame is a fixed 24px inset, so 3 * the 1x default art rect (14,12,298,201) -> (606,36,894,603) stops ten rows short of the real first white row at ~613 and fourteen columns short on the right. It does not matter on this card: the glass ends at y=591 and x=708 in hd pixels, the bg_strip lands at x 729..855, and the patch canvas's own border already measures alpha exactly 0 on every side - so nothing of the element or of its sampling lives in the strip that the short rect excludes. x0=202*3=606 is still the WALL that fences the boy's leg out of the row interpolation, and a wall is a position in the view, which multiplies by 3 like any other.
